objective: Review a Japanese 50-70 second Zundamon/Shikoku-Metan science-news short about the 2026-09-21 Mars Jezero Crater Margin Unit study. Audit factual accuracy, overclaiming, hook quality, and whether the script clearly distinguishes evidence of multiple water-rock alteration episodes from any claim of life detection. Work only from the supplied primary/peer-reviewed evidence. Return concise corrections and a preferred final dialogue order; ChatGPT performs final adjudication. Do not generate media.

shared_evidence.source: NASA/JPL 2026-09-21 — NASA Discovery Reveals Complex Water Systems on Early Mars
shared_evidence.summary: JPL reports Perseverance observations of Jezero Crater's Margin Unit indicate at least three separate episodes of water-rock interaction. Higher exposures are coarse olivine-rich igneous rocks; lower exposures show alteration associated with CO2-rich groundwater, later lake/groundwater processes with silica, and late hot-water/hydrothermal veins including calcium sulfate and fluorite.

shared_evidence.source: Communications Earth & Environment 2026-09-21 — Lake- and groundwater-associated alteration of the olivine-rich Margin unit in Jezero crater, Mars
shared_evidence.summary: The open-access peer-reviewed paper reports three alteration episodes in lower Margin Unit exposures: neutral-to-alkaline CO2-rich fluids forming carbonate ridges; lake/groundwater remobilization with silica precipitation; and late hydrothermal fluids forming fluorite-bearing Ca-sulfate veins. The study describes astrobiological interest but does not report detection of life.

draft_dialogue.caption_text: NASA/JPLが9月21日に紹介した査読研究。PerseveranceのSuperCamでMargin Unitを分析。
